newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Glynhill Int'l buys Asian hotel group.
newsitem.headline: Glynhill Int'l buys Asian hotel group.

text.p: The Lai Sun group's hotel division said on Thursday it is in the final stages of acquiring a majority stake in a group of medium-tariff Asian hotels.

Glynhill International Ltd, which has been renamed and will relist as Lai Sun Hotels International Ltd, announced it had entered into an agreement which would merge the company's Glynhill Hotels and Resorts Ltd and Delta Asia Ltd assets with Century International Hotels Ltd (CIH) of Western Somoa.
The combined value of the assets of the merger company, to be called Sundale Investments Ltd, is HK$352 million, it said. Glynhill's assets are valued at HK$88 million in aggregate.

Glynhill will purchase an additional 26 percent stake in Sundale which, together with its merged hotel holdings, would give it a 51 percent stake in the new company. The cost of the additional stake is HK$91.5 million.

Under the agreement, Glynhill eventually is to acquire the remaining 49 percent stake in Sundale at a cost of 11 times trailing earnings, with the acquisition to be undertaken during the first six months of 2000.
Trading in Glynhill shares, which was suspended on Wednesday pending the merger announcement, resumed on Thursday, rising HK$0.04 to HK$0.63 in early trade.
Glynhill announced previously it had been restructured and renamed Lai Sun Hotel International Limited. It will be relisted on the Hong Kong stock exchange by way of introduction on November 26.
With the merger of the hotel companies, Glynhill parent company Lai Sun Development Ltd said it aims to create a sizeable Asian-based hotel management group.
Lai Sun Development holds 54.1 percent of the issued share capital of Glynhill.

CIH manages more than 3,400 hotel rooms in 12 hotels in Hong Kong, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia and the Philippines and is holding management contracts for an additional 10 hotels with more than 3,000 rooms scheduled to open in 1997 and 1998, it said.

For the two years ended December 1994 and December 1995, CIH had audited profit before tax of about HK$15 million and HK$18 million. As at end-December 1995, the consolidated net tangible assets of CIH were HK$22.7 million.
